initialSourceFindings: The source ASD PVR categories must not be attributed unqualified to the newer 2025 ACC/AHA framework.
The source statement that every sinus venosus lesion requires surgery needs qualification for selected modern transcatheter approaches.
Detailed current AP stages should be checked against the official 2025 classification, not the simplified source summary.
Balloon occlusion is Class 2b in 2025 and can overestimate the actual postclosure wedge-pressure response; question 003 and the new LV-filling assessment question include this limitation.

findings: Caval step-up localizes anomalous venous entry; it does not alone prove an ASD.
Selected superior sinus venosus covered-stent repair requires mapping and unobstructed pulmonary venous redirection.
ASD PVR 5–8 falling below 5 with PAH treatment is a qualified specialist pathway, not a reason to promise cessation of PAH therapy.
High resting left-heart filling pressure is distinct from low-PVR eligibility; balloon-test predictive limits are explicit.
Independent calculation: 125 - 4*(4.5**2) = 44 mmHg RV systolic pressure under the stated assumptions.
Progressive VSD-related aortic regurgitation is a separate assessment indication despite a small shunt.
VSD volume-load closure evaluation requires attributable important/progressive LV enlargement as well as the flow assessment.
2025 VSD treat-and-repair usefulness is uncertain in the specified higher-PVR responder group; the ASD recommendation is not transferred.
Perimembranous closure has a proximal AV-conduction-axis risk distinct from an isolated fascicular lesion.
Left-to-right ductal flow primarily volume-loads LA/LV; a continuous murmur depends on the pressure gradient.
Right-to-left ductal entry beyond the usual left subclavian artery explains differential cyanosis in usual anatomy.
A suitable isolated adult PDA with attributable left-heart enlargement and low PVR favors transcatheter closure; pulmonary vascular disease and test-occlusion limits are qualified.
Postrepair cross-sectional surveillance covers aneurysm and arch anatomy even with a low resting gradient; ESC 2024 gives an adapted 3–5-year interval.
A 7/20 isthmus ratio is 0.35; collaterals can lower a catheter gradient despite important anatomy.
ESC stenting preference is qualified by adult anatomy; current US guidance permits surgical or catheter repair by ACHD experts.
Doppler mean and maximum instantaneous gradients are distinguished from invasive peak-to-peak measurements.
A proximal/distal RV pressure step with little distal-RV-to-PA step localizes intracavitary rather than valvar obstruction.
BAV with aortic dilation prompts first-degree-relative TTE; isolated and concomitant aortic operation thresholds are not conflated.
